subject: IGT optimizer kickoff - do transported gradients pay off at ResNet scale?
body:
Team,

Kicking off the IGT evaluation for trust-theory. Our open-source release implements Implicit Gradient Transport with Anytime Average - reducing variance in online optimization by extrapolating gradients rather than computing them at the current parameter values. The question this project answers for the org: does that variance reduction translate into more predictable, more trustworthy training curves at ResNet scale, or does it stay a theory result?

Scope: run the released resnet_main.py framework, compare IGT against our standard optimizers on convergence variance across seeds, and sweep tail_fraction for the anytime-average window. Deliverable is a recommendation on whether IGT enters the blessed optimizer list.

Milestones inside our short window: framework running by mid-Feb, main comparison done by mid-March, memo by 2026-04-13.

Efe owns methodology, Halima experiments, Emeka and Bilal infra. Bao - resourcing note please.

Ximena
